findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has dead/misleading logic and ignores the feature flag entirely
findings.body: The function reads `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both branches, so it always returns false regardless of the flag. If intentionally disabling the feature, the function should simply return false (or be removed and the check inlined); as written it implies the flag is consulted when it is not, which will confuse future maintainers re-enabling the feature (they will flip the flag expecting it to work).

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is wrong and unhelpful
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression (even one that was previously working with the feature toggle enabled), they get "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature is implemented but disabled; a message like "SQL expressions are disabled" would be accurate and actionable. As written, users and support will misdiagnose the cause.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is not gated by the disable check
findings.body: ReadQuery now returns early for QueryTypeSQL, but the rawNode-based UnmarshalSQLCommand path still constructs a SQLCommand without any feature check. Since sql.TablesList now calls the stub DB which always returns "not implemented", users going through that path get an opaque "error reading SQL command" bad-request error instead of a clear 'feature disabled' message. The gating is inconsistent between the two parsing paths; both should be disabled the same way.

findings.title: TablesList is now guaranteed to fail and still contains the SQL-string-formatting code
findings.body: TablesList calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, which now always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so TablesList can never succeed. The function (including the `fmt.Sprintf` SQL string interpolation it was built around) is effectively dead code reached only via UnmarshalSQLCommand to produce a generic error. It should either be removed or its callers short-circuited so users get a meaningful error.

findings.title: No tests cover the new disabled-SQL behavior
findings.body: The PR changes the behavior of SQL expressions (they now always error) and adds an enableSqlExpressions helper whose return value must stay false for the CVE fix to hold, yet no test is added asserting that a SQL expression query returns an error regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions toggle state. Without a regression test, a future refactor of this confusing helper could silently re-enable the vulnerable code path.
